title: The rook and the bishop
line: Straight lines and diagonals, and what stops them.

steps.text: A rook moves in a straight line along its row or its column, as many squares as it likes, until something is in the way.
Tap every square this rook can reach.
steps.after: It stops before its own pawn. It can capture the black pawn or the knight, but not go past them.

steps.text: Capture the black knight on d2 with the rook.
steps.after: The rook took the knight's square.

steps.text: A bishop moves along diagonals, as many squares as it likes. This one stands on a dark square, so it stays on dark squares.
Tap every square this bishop can reach.
steps.after: Its own pawn blocks one diagonal. It can capture the black pawn, but not reach the king behind it.

steps.text: This bishop moves only on dark squares. Tap the black piece that stands on a light square.

wrong.g5: The rook stands on a dark square, so the bishop can reach it.
wrong.h8: The king stands on a dark square.

steps.after: The knight stands on a light square, where this bishop can never go.

summary: Rooks move along rows and columns, bishops along diagonals. Both stop at the first piece in the way.
